subject: Traffic wave: tail-latency mitigation plan and Dedicated Reserve pilot
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurionhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@aurionhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-14 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Sudden tail-latency spikes during morning traffic wave — can we get immediate mitigation?

Hi Jonas,

We've been seeing pronounced tail-latency spikes (p95->p99) across our core inference calls during the 08:00-10:00 ET window for the past three weekdays. The attached "aurion-prod-latency-graphs.pdf" has the last 7 days sliced by route. This is impacting live triage workflows and a few time-sensitive billing pipelines.

Ask: can Redwood confirm what changed on the serving side and provide a short-term mitigation (routing, cache warm, or config change) while we discuss more durable options? Also, we need to understand how this affects renewal discussions — if spikes continue we will need tighter uptime guarantees or a discount path.

We are prepared to explore a Dedicated Reserve pilot if that can materially reduce variance. What's the earliest timeline for a pilot and what commercial commitments would be expected?

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Ops
Aurion Health

Attachment: aurion-prod-latency-graphs.pdf (7 pages)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-14 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden tail-latency spikes during morning traffic wave — can we get immediate mitigation?

Maya — thanks for the quick flag and the graphs, that was helpful.

Short answer: we can put in a three-stage plan immediately while we scope a Dedicated Reserve pilot.

1) Immediate mitigations (next 24 hours):
- Temporary traffic shaping: route high-volume low-priority routes to the lower-cost replica pool to reduce burst contention.
- Increase KV cache TTL for your most common prefixes to reduce repeated decode work during the window.
- Apply an aggressive batching window (20ms) for the morning window to smooth bursts.

2) Rapid operational controls (3–7 days):
- Schedule a config change with our infra team to pin a subset of your traffic to instances with higher I/O reservation.
- Deploy a short-lived warm-up load to populate KV caches before the window.

3) Durable option — Dedicated Reserve pilot (2–4 weeks to stand up):
- Proposal: 2 x reserved GPU pods sized to your peak concurrency with network isolation and priority routing.
- Measurable SLOs: targeted p99 latency drop by 30–50% in the morning window, and separate error budget accounting for the pilot.

We will also open a postmortem ticket to look for any runtime regressions in the last deploy window. Marissa — can you pull a pilot commercial stub and a short SOW for timelines/cost? Sergio — will you own the infra changes and confirm there are no platform-wide regressions that would block the short-term fixes?

Maya, I'll schedule a 30-min call for this afternoon to agree next steps.

—Jonas
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurionhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15 08:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Traffic wave — pilot commercial outline and SOW draft

Maya — attaching a short commercial outline and SOW draft (pilot-sow-draft.docx) and a proposed configuration workbook (proposed-dedicated-config.xlsx).

Quick notes on commercial approach so we can be aligned for renewal discussions:
- Pilot term: 30 days (production pilot with metrics collection).
- Pilot fee: one-time setup + prorated reserved capacity fee. Will provide two options: (A) month-to-month reserved capacity with priority routing; (B) 6-month commitment with discounted unit price and integrated SLO credits if we miss agreed p99 targets during the commitment term.
- Renewal linkage: if Aurion converts to a longer-term Dedicated contract within 60 days after a successful pilot, we can fold pilot fees into first invoice and offer an onboarding discount; if there is an ongoing reliability issue during renewal window, we are open to an SLA credit structure as part of negotiations.

Requested: Maya, can you confirm which commercial option you want us to model and whether legal should see the SOW now or after pilot acceptance?

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: pilot-sow-draft.docx; proposed-dedicated-config.xlsx
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@aurionhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@aurionhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-20 14:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Traffic wave — pilot commercial outline and SOW draft

Thanks, Marissa / Jonas.

We reviewed the SOW and config workbook with our infra team. We're prepared to accept the 30-day pilot (Option A) with the following conditions before we go live:

- An explicit uptime commitment for the pilot window: >= 99.5% availability for request success (we'll use your tracing to verify).
- If during the pilot our p99 latency does not improve by at least 30% in the morning window, we want a defined remediation credit that can be applied to our renewal or onboarding invoice.
- A rollback/fallback policy: if Dedicated Reserve causes any cascading errors for our other routes, Redwood must immediately fall back to the shared pool routing for the impacted routes for the duration of the incident.

If Redwood can accept those conditions, we will sign the pilot SOW and schedule the production cutover one week from acceptance. We need this timeline in order to align a product release that's reliant on the improved latency.

Maya
Head of Platform Ops
Aurion Health
